scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they lost all reach across the
data-center fabric -- pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) is unreachable, though pc_0_0
can still ping its own gateway 10.0.0.1. The NOC adds that both
spine routers reported their BGP session toward leaf_router_0_0 going
down at the same moment, while the leaf's uplink interfaces still
show UP. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and watchfrr) on leaf_router_0_0

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_0 bgpd
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_0 is the top-of-rack leaf for pc_0_0
  (host subnet 10.0.0.0/24 on eth2). Its only fabric attachment is
  EBGP: neighbor 172.16.0.4 (spine_router_0_0, AS 65100) on eth0 and
  neighbor 172.16.0.8 (spine_router_0_1, AS 65101) on eth1. With bgpd
  dead the leaf stops learning 10.0.1.0/24 and stops advertising
  10.0.0.0/24, so pc_0_0 is isolated from the fabric even though every
  physical link is still UP.
Localization: leaf_router_0_0
Root cause: bgpd not running on leaf_router_0_0
Fix: restart FRR on leaf_router_0_0 (`service frr restart`) -- this lab
  keeps its config in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so a restart fully restores
  the BGP configuration and sessions.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03 on this fabric): bgpd is killed
together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh
remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO
`router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent
may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is
missing/empty on leaf_router_0_0" -- that is the same fault observed at
the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
`service frr restart` on leaf_router_0_0. Unlike the vtysh-configured
kath labs, this lab has a persistent /etc/frr/frr.conf, so the restart
brings bgpd back WITH its full BGP configuration; the sessions to both
spines re-establish and pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 again.
scoring_axes: bonus-exonerates-fabric: notes the spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 are healthy (their other sessions stay Established), so the fault is only on leaf_router_0_0

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: FRRouting (BGP control plane) on leaf_router_0_0. The data-plane interfaces remain UP, but the routing process is down.

Mechanism: pc_0_0’s traffic to 10.0.1.2 is forwarded to its default gateway (10.0.0.1 on leaf_router_0_0). With BGP down on that leaf, it has no route to the remote subnet 10.0.1.0/24, so it immediately generates ICMP “Destination Net Unreachable,” matching the user report. Meanwhile, the spines lose their BGP sessions to this leaf at the same time, even though the physical links are still up.

Localization and evidence:
- From pc_0_0 to 10.0.1.2: “From 10.0.0.1 Destination Net Unreachable” (icmp errors from the leaf).
- leaf_router_0_0 interfaces are UP with correct IPs (eth0 172.16.0.5/31, eth1 172.16.0.9/31, eth2 10.0.0.1/24).
- On leaf_router_0_0: “bgpd is not running” and systemctl shows “frr.service … Active: inactive (dead).”
- On both spines, BGP neighbors to 172.16.0.5 and 172.16.0.9 are in “Active” (not established), while sessions to other devices remain up.

Root cause: The FRR service on leaf_router_0_0 stopped (crashed or was administratively stopped), bringing down both BGP sessions simultaneously.

Corrective fix: Restart and enable FRR on leaf_router_0_0 (systemctl start frr; ensure it’s enabled). Verify proper BGP configuration is present (AS, neighbors to both spines) and sessions establish. Confirm routes to 10.0.1.0/24 appear and end-to-end pings between pc_0_0 and pc_0_1 succeed. Review logs to prevent recurrence.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly localizes the failure to leaf_router_0_0 (FRR/BGP control plane on that device), matching the required device identification.
The agent explicitly states bgpd/FRR (the BGP daemon) is not running on leaf_router_0_0 and attributes the outage to the stopped/crashed FRR service, matching the required identification.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-fabric: notes the spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 are healthy (their other sessions stay Established), so the fault is only on leaf_router_0_0
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly notes both spines’ other BGP sessions remain established (sessions to other devices stay up), indicating the fault is isolated to leaf_router_0_0 and exonerating the fabric.
The agent recommends restarting/enabling the FRR service and verifying BGP configuration and routes, which matches the expected fix to restore bgpd and re-establish sessions.

The log clearly shows pc traffic gets ICMP 'Destination Net Unreachable' from the leaf, bgpd is not running and frr.service is inactive on leaf_router_0_0, and the running-config lacks BGP—these observations justify the conclusion that the FRR/BGP process on the leaf is down and causing the loss of routes. The investigator’s inferences follow logically and the suggested restart fix matches the observed root cause.
